html:
French chemist and microbiologist who showed that germs cause disease and make food go bad. He made vaccines for anthrax and rabies, and gave his name to pasteurisation.

He began in chemistry, studying crystals. Asked to help brewers and winemakers, he showed that fermentation is the work of living microbes, and that wine and beer spoil because of the wrong ones. Gentle heating killed them, the method now called pasteurisation, used for milk. With experiments on sealed flasks he showed that microbes come from other microbes, not from nothing.

This led to the germ theory of disease, which he and the German doctor Robert Koch proved in the 1870s and 1880s. It changed medicine, surgery and hygiene.

Building on Jenner's smallpox vaccine, he found how to weaken germs to make vaccines. He tested an anthrax vaccine on sheep in 1881, and in 1885 saved a boy bitten by a rabid dog. The Pasteur Institute opened in Paris in 1888. His work also explained why canning keeps food safe.
sum: French chemist and microbiologist who showed that germs cause disease and make food go bad. He made vaccines for anthrax and rabies, and gave his name to pasteurisation.
